entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 28/05/2022, the learned Special Judge, Schedule Caste/Schedule Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities)Act/Additional Sessions Judge (FTC), Raigarh in Sessions Trial No. 23/2020 has convicted the appellants for the offence punishable under Sections 376 D of the IPC and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment for the remaining life and to pay fine of Rs. 60,000/-, in default of payment of fine to further undergo RI for 1 year.

entities.text: Special Judge, Schedule Caste/Schedule Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities)Act/Additional Sessions Judge (FTC), Raigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Mr. Sanjay Agrawal, learned counsel for the appellant in Cr.A. No. 963/2022, Mr. Awadh Tripathi and Mr. Dheerendra Pandey, learned counsel for appellants in Cr.A. No. 1147/2022.
Also heard Mr. Gurudev I. Sharan, Govt. Advocate, appearing for the respondent/State on the instant applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (I.A. No. 1 of 2022 in both the cases).

Learned counsel for the convicts/appellants have argued that though the appellants were named in the FIR, from the statement of the prosecutrix (PW1) who is a married lady, it is apparent that she did not knew the appellants before.
Neither she named the appellants nor the Test Identification Parade was conducted in order to identify the culprits of the offence.

It is submitted that from the statement of the prosecutrix (PW1), it is apparent that the police personnel have introduced the present appellants being the accused for committing the crime, thus, the appellants have been falsely implicated in the present case.
Even the FSL report is negative.
It is further argued that the appellants have no criminal antecedents, therefore, they may be released on bail.
An objection has been filed on behalf of the State/respondent.

Mr. Gurudev I. Sharan, Govt.
Advocate appearing for the State/respondent formally opposes the prayer for grant of bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended with the bail application.

Taking into the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly the fact no Test Identification Parade was conducted and FSL report is negative and, we deem it appropriate to allow the applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellants.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellants by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.

They shall be released on bail on their executing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand Only) each with one surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for their appearance before the Registry of this Court on 20.09.2023.

They shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to them by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.

Consequently, I.A. Nos.
1 of 2022 filed in Cr.A. No. 963/2022 and 1147/2022 are allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only confined for disposal of aforesaid I.A. filed in these appeals and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List these matters for final hearing.
C.C. as per rules.
 Sd/- Sd/-
